prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts the camera wearer looking down at a freshly plastered concrete ledge and metal grid structure in the immediate foreground (brightest white/light grey, ~0.2–0.8 m away), while the sloped dirt embankment, bricks, and vegetation behind and above it recede to ~1.5–4.0 m (dark grey to black). In frames 1–4, the wearer's left hand resting on top of the ledge (~0.3–0.5 m) and right forearm holding a trowel at the right corner (~0.3–0.6 m, ~0.3–0.4 m to the right of the left hand) are within arm's reach, and in frame 5 the viewpoint turns leftward and downward to show the wearer's own torso/shoulder at the bottom (~0.2 m), the concrete block stretching forward (~0.4–1.2 m), and a second person's lower legs and feet standing on the left (~1.0–1.5 m away, ~0.3 m left of the block, facing roughly rightward/sideways and cropped above the knees so their head and gaze direction are out of view). Across frames 1–4, the right forearm and trowel move slightly upward and forward along the corner of the concrete structure before the sharp leftward camera turn and downward pitch in frame 5 shifts the metal grid out of view to the right and brings the ground and second person's feet into view on the left. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map more clearly separates the elevated foreground concrete block and arms from the shadowed recess beneath the ledge and the sloping dirt background despite harsh dappled sunlight. However, the map is unreliable along the thin wire mesh of the right-hand metal grid—where background depths bleed through and fill the open squares inconsistently—and in frame 5 where the sunlit dirt and the side of the concrete block merge into a smooth gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is entirely blank in frame 1, detects only the camera wearer's right arm and hand as 'person' in the lower-right foreground (~0.3–0.6 m away) of frames 2–4, and in frame 5 labels a fragmented pink 'person' region on the lower left (~0.5–1.5 m away) while missing all other scene elements. Across frames 2–4, this segmented right forearm shifts slightly upward and inward toward the upper-right edge of the concrete ledge (which lies ~0.4–0.6 m in front of the wearer), before vanishing in frame 5 when the camera turns left and the right hand holding the trowel moves to the bottom-right corner. In frame 5, the single 'person' mask on the left erroneously merges part of the second person's lower legs and sandals (~1.2 m away on the left ground), a wooden post, and the shadowed left vertical face of the concrete wall (~0.5–1.0 m in front) into one silhouette, while the wearer's own shoulder at the bottom edge (~0.2 m) and right hand go undetected. This map adds almost nothing beyond the RGB strip except confirming the foreground contour of the right forearm in frames 2–4, and it is highly unreliable because it completely misses the wearer's left arm in frames 1–4 (within ~0.3–0.5 m on the left), the trowel, the concrete structure, the metal grid, and the actual body boundaries in frame 5. Because only limbs and false wall regions are segmented and all heads are out of the camera's field of view, facing and gaze directions cannot be determined from the segmentation masks.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any yellow body keypoints or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the sequence. From the RGB strip context, the camera wearer's left hand rests on the concrete ledge (~0.3–0.5 m in front and to the left) and the right hand manipulates a trowel (~0.3–0.6 m in front and to the right, ~0.3–0.4 m apart) within arm's reach across frames 1–4, while frame 5 turns left to show the wearer's lower torso (~0.2 m below), right hand at the bottom-right edge (~0.3 m), and another person's lower legs standing ~1.0–1.5 m away on the left (~0.3 m from the concrete block). Both the camera wearer's head/upper torso and the second person's upper body and head are completely occluded or outside the field of view in all frames, so neither person's head orientation or gaze toward the camera wearer is visible even in RGB, though the wearer's arms extend forward from the viewpoint and the second person's feet point roughly rightward toward the concrete structure. Because the pose estimator outputs no skeletons at all, it provides no spatial information beyond the RGB image and is completely unreliable under these egocentric viewing angles, heavy self-occlusion/truncation of bodies at the frame borders, and dark skin tones against dark wet concrete.
